title: podman run with cgroups=split flake - controller `pids` is not available

comments.body: A friendly reminder that this issue had no activity for 30 days.

Hey @Luap99, I dug into this one. Can I try to solve this and raise a PR ? 

The test in `test/e2e/run_test.go` wraps podman with `systemd-run --scope` (+ `--user` for rootless), but it doesn't pass `--property=Delegate=yes`. In cgroup v2, without explicit delegation on the scope unit, systemd doesn't guarantee that controllers like `pids` will be written to `cgroup.subtree_control` for child cgroups. Whether they show up depends on the systemd user session state at that moment, which explains why it's flaky rather than consistently broken.
When `--cgroups=split` runs, Podman creates `libpod-payload-<id>` directly under the caller's cgroup (`getOCICgroupPath()` in `libpod/container_internal_linux.go`), and `crun` then expects `pids` to be available in `cgroup.controllers` there. Without delegation it sometimes isn't.
The fix should be straightforward as adding `"--property=Delegate=yes"` to `scopeOptions.Wrapper` in the test. This is also what Quadlet does (`service.Add(ServiceGroup, "Delegate", "yes")` in `pkg/systemd/quadlet/quadlet.go`) for the same reason.

@giuseppe ^^ WDYT?

I would have assumed that would cause a hard failure consistently and not flake but I am don't know the systemd details.
